data.claim: With two clones writing as `sameid`, A's merged shard reads [1,2,3,4,2]; the tail-read clock hands the next append lamport 3, so `update X1 --title v5` folds to v4, doctor is silent, and two clones in same-named dirs derive the same id. Scanning every parsed event instead costs ~7 ms per append at 20k events with the warm read cache.
data.falsifier: The merged shard's tail equals its max, or the v5 update folds last, or the warm scan costs more than ~20 ms per append at 20k events.
data.mechanism: _highest_lamport trusts each shard's last line as its max, which holds only for a single writer; merge=union writes OURS then THEIRS, so another clone's low-clock suffix lands at the tail. default_agent_id is {host}-{tree name}, identical across same-named clones on same-named hosts. _read_shard re-parses only appended bytes after a sha256 prefix check.

ddflow brief --item B190 read; AGENTS.md managed block read; recall surfaced Re770238400, B28589b8b26, B54 (head() one-pass), lesson L5808fe73f8 (not applicable). Constraints carried: no dir created on EventLog construction; identity must agree between claim and commit hook across worktrees (repo_root = primary checkout).

data.alternatives: Keep the tail read and detect non-monotone shards separately: impossible without reading the whole shard anyway. Store the suffix in the git common dir: per-clone too, but the task and .ddflow/local's gitignore already cover it and repo_root always resolves to the primary checkout. Keep the legacy id when a legacy shard exists: a fresh clone contains the other clone's legacy shard, so it would reproduce the collision. Doctor PROBLEM for a decreasing shard: the log is append-only, so doctor could never pass again.
data.consequences: Derived ids change once on upgrade (old shards stay readable; a lease held under the old derived id across the upgrade no longer reads as the same agent until it is re-claimed or expires). Appends read every shard's bytes (sha256 prefix check) instead of a tail: O(bytes) I/O per append, notable on NFS.
data.context: Two clones with the same hostname and directory name (or the same DDFLOW_AGENT) wrote one shard; merge=union interleaved their clocks and the tail-read clock regressed, losing the newest edit (B28589b8b26).
data.decision: (1) Once .ddflow/ exists, the derived id is {host}-{tree}-{suffix}; suffix = 6 hex chars in <primary checkout>/.ddflow/local/clone-id, created once by hard-linking a written temp file, never rewritten; local/ gets its own `*` .gitignore. Explicit, env and config ids are never suffixed. (2) EventLog._highest_lamport takes max over _read_shard events of every shard (parse cache keeps it ~7 ms at 20k events). (3) doctor reports a shard whose clock decreases in file order as a NOTE naming the shard and event number.
data.title: Derived agent ids carry a per-clone suffix; the Lamport clock is the max over every parsed event; a decreasing shard is a doctor NOTE

data.body: B190 appends a per-clone suffix to derived agent ids ({host}-{tree} -> {host}-{tree}-{hex6}). A lease claimed before the upgrade under the bare derived id stays live, but after the upgrade every holder comparison (leases.renew/_transition, api/gates.py:221, api/jobs.py:51, core/schedule.py:412/421) sees it as someone else's: heartbeat says 'no lease held', complete/merge refuse, claim refuses. The commit hook is fine (enforce.py same_tree rule). Workaround today: release/re-claim with --agent <old id> (as_agent over MCP). Fix: treat the bare derived id of THIS clone as an alias of the suffixed one for leases whose holder equals it, only when this clone has no shard/lease under the suffixed id for that item — and say so in `ddflow identify`. Regression test: claim under the bare id, create .ddflow/local/clone-id, heartbeat must succeed.
data.title: Upgrade path for B190: a lease held under the pre-suffix derived id is not "mine" after upgrade

With commit_without_lease=block it refuses. Probe: claim X --globs a; update X --globs a,b; commit b.

Only other max-lamport is core/model.py fold's st.last_lamport (pure fold, different role). infra/tomlcfg.atomic_write is last-writer-wins via os.replace, the wrong semantics for create-once (two racers would keep different suffixes), so _clone_suffix does not duplicate it.

data.summary: B190 pre-merge: EventLog.__init__ derives its id eagerly, so a read-only log of a sibling repo (services/external.sync, documented 'never writing there') creates <sibling>/.ddflow/local/clone-id. Found by the bug-hunt subagent, probe: external.sync over a sibling with only .ddflow/events -> sibling gains local/.

data.rule: Any O(1) summary read from an append-only file's tail (clock, counter, high-water mark) is valid only under a single-writer invariant. If the file is ever combined by merge=union, sync, or copy from another clone, that invariant is gone and nothing on disk records it: derive the summary from the whole (cached) content, and make identities that name a writer unique per clone, not just per host and directory.
data.title: A 'last line is the max' shortcut only holds while a file has exactly one writer; merge=union silently gives it two
